Ruling: model error; the page does not state this helper: it is true when any situation the tool refuses for Schedule 3 lines 6a to 6z, 12 and 13a to 13z, or for a foreign tax credit carried from another year, is present, and the five credit limit worksheet lines refuse on it (i1040s8812 p. 4, Credit Limit Worksheet A, line 2; i8863 p. 8, line 5; i5695 pp. 5 and 7, line 2 of each worksheet). The project reads each situation's gate line in asking order as a chain of two-way chooses. The reply reads the questions directly as one `any` and, as its note says, covers only the situations of lines 6a to 6m: it leaves out the kerosene claim of line 12, the line 13 situations and the foreign tax carryover. executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/s3.json`, pass bcb756ef462c; 1,854 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 616 partial records from 40 bases; 2,969 comparisons): 2,732 agree; 228 project-unknown (156 on incomplete and 72 on refused returns), where the chain stops at the first unanswered situation (spec 4.7.3) and the reply's disjunction is decided by a later one; 9 value differences, all on refused returns, project true and reply false: the witnesses are the fixtures ss.other.components (kerosene), redesign.credits.refuse.farmland, redesign.credits.refuse.ftc_carryover, redesign.credits.refuse.section960c, redesign.credits.refuse.section965 and redesign.credits.refuse.virgin_islands, each a situation the reply leaves out and each refused by the situation's own gate under either reading. None on a completed return. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; f1040s3 line 2, "Credit for child and dependent care expenses from Form 2441, line 11. Attach Form 2441", and i2441 p. 1, Purpose of Form: "If you paid someone to care for your child or other qualifying person so you (or your spouse if filing jointly) could work or look for work in 2025, you may be able to take the credit". A filer with no care expenses takes no credit and needs no Form 2441 Part II; the project guards on f2441.care, the candidate copies f2441.line11 on every return. executable-triage-v2 (triage/s3.json; 1,306 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 120 partial records from 40 bases; 1,926 comparisons): 409 of 1,926 agree; 1,517 differ, 760 candidate-unknown (394 on completed returns, e.g. classm.s8812.4.deepseek and classm.f5695.3.deepseek to .6.deepseek: project $0.00, the candidate stops on the care-provider roster $dcprov) and 757 candidate-refuses, all on refused returns (classm.w2.1.deepseek, f2441.line14_bad; classm.f4952.3.deepseek, f2441.student_disabled); no value differs. The interface offers f2441.care: not an interface gap. Unchanged by Stage 19; same ruling as Stage 18. Project stands.

Ruling: model error; f1040s3 line 3, "Education credits from Form 8863, line 19", and i1040gi p. 115, Line 3: "If you (or your dependent) paid qualified expenses in 2025 for yourself, your spouse, or your dependent to enroll in or attend an eligible educational institution, you may be able to take an education credit. See Form 8863 for details. However, you can’t take an education credit if any of the following applies. • You, or your spouse if filing jointly, are claimed as a dependent on someone else’s (such as your parent’s) 2025 tax return"; i8863 p. 3, Who cannot claim a credit, "1. You’re claimed as a dependent on another person’s tax return". The project enters Form 8863 line 19 only when f8863.eligible (f8863.paid yes and sli.claimed no; married filing separately and nonresident aliens are refused for the whole return by s3.mfs and scope.other_income) and zero otherwise; the candidate copies line 19 on every return, so Form 8863 (its line 3 refusal sa.excluded_income, its Credit Limit Worksheet) is evaluated for filers who paid no education expenses. executable-triage-v2 (triage/s3.json; 1,306 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 120 partial records from 40 bases; 1,926 comparisons): 415 of 1,926 agree; 1,511 differ, 784 candidate-unknown (394 on completed returns) and 727 candidate-refuses, all on refused returns (classm.w2.1.deepseek; classm.f8889.4.deepseek, sa.excluded_income; classm.f4952.3.deepseek); no value differs. Traced (triage.py --explain 3 --witness 7, classm.s8812.4.deepseek, f8863.paid no, project $0.00): every candidate Form 8863 line is $0.00 up to Credit Limit Worksheet line 5, which reads the candidate's own Schedule 3 line 2 (the unguarded Form 2441 copy) and stops on $dcprov, so on the completed-return witnesses the unknown is inherited from the candidate's line 2; the candidate's own error on line 3 is that it asks Form 8863 of every filer and refuses excluded-income filers who claim no credit. Where both compute, the values agree: Form 8863's own zeros for an ineligible return (lines 1 and 10 choose f8863.zero) are not disputed. The pages given (f1040s3, f1040, i1040gi pp. 14 and 117) do not include p. 115, but the published interface offers f8863.eligible: not an interface gap. Checked against the source: the eligible gate is p. 115's first bar; the second and fourth are whole-return refusals; the third (line 11b at or above $90,000 or $180,000) is Form 8863 line 4's stop (line 4 zero makes lines 7 and 18 zero). Project stands.

Ruling: model error; as the earlier rulings on this line. f1040s3 line 5a, "Residential clean energy credit from Form 5695, line 15". The project takes Form 5695 line 15 when f5695.part1_any is Yes and $0 otherwise; the reply copies f5695.line15 on every return, so it needs Part I answers (f5695.business_use, f5695.construction_later) the interview asks only after a Yes, or refuses at Part I gates the project never reaches. The rewording of part1_any and line 5a (BUG-0552, BUG-0553) changes no value. Re-reviewed because f5695.part1_any, which this line reads, was reworded so that the one spouse phrase governs the 2024 carryforward as well as the costs (wording only; no expression changed). The disagreement is the one ruled before on this line, in the words above: the candidate's expression and the project's are both unchanged from that ruling. executable-triage-v2 (`.transcription/triage/2025/s3.json`, pass 56fd9caa95a1; 1,767 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 120 partial records; every completed witness listed by a scratch rerun with the witness cap lifted): 1,240 of 2,387 comparisons agree; differences by kind {"candidate-refuses": 859, "candidate-unknown": 288}; on completed returns {"candidate-refuses": 1, "candidate-unknown": 119} (the candidate refuses at f5695.construction_later on 1; the candidate is unknown for f5695.business_use, f5695.construction_later on 119). The other differences are on refused or incomplete returns. No change to the data.

Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 117, Line 9: "Complete Form 8962 to determine the amount of your premium tax credit, if any. If the premium tax credit you can claim exceeds your advance credit payments, your net premium tax credit will be shown on Form 8962, line 26. Enter that amount, if any, on line 9". The project enters zero when no Form 1095-A is listed (f8962.any, written out by the comparison as a count of f1095a entries; i8962 p. 3, Who Must File); the candidate copies Form 8962 line 26 on every return, so a filer with no Marketplace coverage must answer Form 8962's questions. executable-triage-v2 (triage/s3.json; 1,306 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 120 partial records from 40 bases; 1,926 comparisons): 564 of 1,926 agree; 1,362 differ, 1,129 candidate-unknown (470 on completed returns, classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .6.deepseek: f8962.alloc unanswered, project $0.00) and 233 candidate-refuses, all on refused returns (classm.dependent.2.deepseek, .4, .5); no value differs. The interface offers f8962.any: not an interface gap. Unchanged by Stage 19; same ruling as Stage 18. Project stands.
